Pricing

What goes into a custom gift box price?

FORME Packaging editorialUpdated October 21, 20263 min read

Price follows the specification. Dimensions, construction, print coverage, finishing and packing can change the work involved even when two boxes look similar online.

In this guideSize and structure shape the starting costSeparate printing from finishingUnderstand quantity and setupCompare the complete delivered scopeDiscuss your packaging →

Size and structure shape the starting cost

A larger box consumes more board and wrapping paper and occupies more shipping volume. Depth matters as well as length and width: a deep base changes the wall area, wrapping operation and insert requirements. Avoid comparing unit prices using only a product photograph.

Construction introduces different operations. A rigid drawer needs a fitted tray and sleeve; a magnetic box adds a connected cover and closure; a collapsible box has folding panels and corner assembly. A printed white-card carton uses a different converting process. The appropriate comparison is the completed specification, rather than a broad label such as “luxury box.”

Separate printing from finishing

Record whether the exterior, interior or both are printed. Identify any spot colors, foil areas, embossing positions and special papers. A small foil mark and an all-over metallic design may require different tooling and handling. Very fine lines and large solids also need suitable paper and proofing.

Ask what is included in the quoted finish. The paper texture, coating and foil can influence appearance together. Confirm the desired result on a sample instead of adding several processes simply because they are available.

Understand quantity and setup

Custom tools, artwork preparation and production setup may be spread across the order. Ask for quotations at realistic volume breaks for the same dimensions and artwork. Splitting one order into several sizes or designs can alter the comparison.

Keep sampling, dies, printing plates and freight visible in the quotation. Clarify which charges are one-time, which recur on reorders, and what happens if the structure or artwork changes. The website estimator is only a planning illustration; it does not replace a supplier quotation.

Compare the complete delivered scope

  • Unit price and quantity for each size and design.
  • Insert, ribbon, tissue and other accessories included.
  • Sampling and tooling scope with change allowances.
  • Flat or assembled supply and outer packing method.
  • Freight terms, destination and any excluded charges.

If a proposal is cheaper, ask which specification choices differ. It may be possible to simplify a finish, improve the product arrangement or reduce excess space while retaining the intended presentation. Send the same written brief to each supplier and compare the answers line by line.
